messages:
emily: Heads-up — product plans to GA Stratus-Neo next week. Asking for quick impact estimate on token/sec and GPU-hours so we can size Dedicated pools and pre-warm.
ajay: Do we have expected qps or customer beta telemetry?
dylan: Beta has been small but latency-sensitive. Expect ~20k qps at peak across hosted API (mostly chat). Model is 2.1x cost vs current baseline per token.
emily: Product expects a staged rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 days. Peak day traffic likely during business hours PST.
kai: Rough numbers: Stratus-Neo median output length ~220 tokens, request input ~80 tokens, so ~300 tokens per request. If 20k qps -> 6M tokens/sec. That seems high, double-checking.
ajay: Wait 20k qps * 300 tokens = 6M tokens/s yes. But the 20k qps is global; region split: 60% US, 30% EU, 10% APAC.
emily: We shouldn't assume all requests hit the largest model; product plans to send heavier workloads to Neo but fallback to Neo-Base for low-tier customers. Rollout will map 25% of requests to Neo-Base variant.
dylan: Ok let's compute steady-state GPU hours for peak hour. Empirical throughput: one A100-80 can do ~120k tokens/s for this model (quantized). Using that: GPUs_needed = ceil(6_000_000 / 120_000) = 50 GPUs. Accounting for 25% on Neo-Base reduces load to 4.5M tokens/s -> 38 GPUs.
kai: Add buffer for burst/overhead and autoscaler granularity -> we should request 50 GPUs in Dedicated pool US region for safety. EU needs 30% of that -> 15 GPUs. APAC -> 5 GPUs. Total ~70 GPUs.
ajay: Ops note: current free capacity in US Dedicated pool is 12 GPUs; need +38 reserved ahead of launch. Lead time for provisioning in that cluster is ~48 hours (driver/cuda images, node prepping).
emily: Cost check: estimated GPU-hour cost (cloud) $3.5/hr per GPU after discounts. If we run 70 GPUs for 4 peak hours/day during launch -> 70*4*3.5 = $980/day (but multiply by baseline continuous background usage). Also consider spike mitigation fallback to Neo-Base to save cost.
dylan: Also network egress could be heavy if we stream outputs. Average response size ~2KB -> at 20k qps that's 40MB/s -> ~144GB/hr -> ~0.14TB/hr per region at peak. Not huge but keep an eye for EU inter-region routing.
kai: Ops-bot: running quick synthetic to simulate autoscaler behavior...
ops-bot: ```simulate_autoscale --model stratus-neo --qps 20000 --tokens_per_req 300 --fallback_ratio 0.25 --region-split 60,30,10 --result GPUs_US:50 GPUs_EU:15 GPUs_APAC:5```
ajay: The simulate_autoscale output aligns with manual calc. Action items: 1) Reserve US +38 GPUs in Dedicated pool by EOD. 2) Prep EU +15, APAC +5 on standby (soft reservation). 3) Add pre-warm job to seed KV caches 2 hours before rollouts.
emily: Also add canary policy: route 1% traffic to Neo for first 30m, monitor p99 latency and error rate. Auto rollback threshold: p99 > 1.5x baseline or errors > 0.5%.
dylan: For capacity planning doc, I'll add two scenarios: conservative (50% higher qps) and optimistic (25% lower qps) with GPU-hour breakdown.
kai: Quick note on quantization: if we switch to 4-bit int8-style pipeline can increase per-GPU throughput by ~1.6x; that could reduce GPUs in US from 50->31. Need perf validation and regen tests.
ajay: We should not rely on quantization for GA; treat as mitigation after launch if latency/cost is worse than expected.
emily: Final: please drop a short snippet into Launch Runbook and add cost estimate to finance slack. I'll file the reservation ticket now. :thumbsup:
